findings.evidence: Lines 323–346 show `firstOrder_mk`/`hessian_mk` use `WithLp.fst/snd (W2p.mk …).1`; only those two carry `@[simp]`, whereas the analogous `W1p.value_mk` and `W1p.gradient_mk` at W1p.lean:446 and :452 are both public-accessor statements marked `@[simp]`.
findings.fix: State `firstOrder_mk` and `hessian_mk` directly as `W2p.firstOrder (W2p.mk …) = u` and `W2p.hessian (W2p.mk …) = H`, and mark all four public `*_mk` accessor lemmas `@[simp]`.
findings.issue: `W2p.firstOrder_mk` and `W2p.hessian_mk` state elimination through `WithLp.fst/snd` and `.1`, while `W2p.value_mk` and `gradient_mk` lack `@[simp]`; users cannot uniformly simplify `W2p`'s public accessors after `mk` without relying on representation lemmas.

summary: The constructor elimination API exposes representation details and lacks consistent simplification rules.
